title: Where a dragged pane is dropped decides how it joins the layout
body:
A pane drag (`Drag::Pane` in `src/compositor.rs`) can only swap: dropping on another pane calls `Layout::swap`, which exchanges the two leaf ids in the split tree. The target pane gets a cyan outline while the pointer is over it.

## Proposal

Where the pointer is when the drag ends decides the drop:

| Zone | Drop |
|---|---|
| middle half of a pane, both ways | swap with that pane |
| rest of a pane, nearest edge wins | split that pane on that side; the dragged pane takes the half on that side |
| two-cell band along a window edge | split the root on that side; the dragged pane spans that side and takes a third |
| the dragged pane's own slot | nothing |

While a ghost is held, a cyan rectangle with a translucent fill and a short label ("swap", "left", "right", "above", "below") covers the rect the dragged pane would get. decade gets that rect by applying the drop to a copy of the tree and arranging it.

## Rejected

- Dropping in the gutter between two panes to insert between them. Jack tried it on 2026-11-06 and chose edge zones instead.
